title: All the key moments from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli claimed his eighth win of the season at the Spanish Grand Prix, the Mercedes driver extending his points lead in the title race as Formula 1 made its first visit to the Madring.

Although the Italian came out on top on the streets of Madrid, Lando Norris lost a potential victory due to an ill-timed Virtual Safety Car, while Lewis Hamilton's race was over almost before it started after brake problems.

Here are all the key moments from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix…

Antonelli extends lead to 81 points after another victory

Kimi Antonelli put in yet another impressive display to become the first driver to take victory at the Madring, and record his eighth win of the season from 14 Grands Prix.

The Mercedes racer continues to march on in his quest for a maiden F1 title, with his margin over team mate George Russell now standing at 81 points.

Antonelli didn't really put a foot wrong all weekend, but was no match for Lando Norris' pace in the early stages of Sunday's race after starting second.

A short Virtual Safety Car deployment just as Antonelli headed to the pit entrance allowed him to take a cheap pit stop, as Norris missed his chance in the pivotal moment of the race.

Once Charles Leclerc's Ferrari made a late pit stop from the lead, Antonelli was back in front but acknowledged that Norris had been the quickest driver on the day.

“It’s good to win, but it doesn’t feel as good because I think Lando today deserved to win," said Antonelli.

In contrast, Russell was left to finish only P5 having made one extra stop than those ahead after being left compromised by starting in P6.

The Briton admitted post-race that any hopes of challenging Antonelli for the drivers' title had all but faded with nine Grands Prix still remaining.

"Realistically, I’m not in the fight for the drivers’ [title]," he said. "That just allows me to focus race by race and try to get some good results."

Antonelli insists Norris 'deserved to win' Spanish GP

Norris' Qualifying heroics undone by VSC

Just in case his victories in Hungary and the Netherlands weren’t enough to demonstrate the calibre of driver Lando Norris has become, the reigning World Champion executed what he confessed was “one of the best laps” of his F1 career in Qualifying.

With the exception of a small error at the final turn, the Briton mastered the latest addition to the calendar to edge out Mercedes’ Antonelli by 0.011s for his third pole position in four races.

With overtaking spots limited, it gave the McLaren driver a real chance of victory come race day.

And he got off to a confident start, rebuffing Antonelli's challenge when the lights went out, with the Italian making two small mistakes that enabled Norris to quickly build a lead at the front.

It was a somewhat cruel irony that soon after his engineer praised him for managing his tyres so well, the Virtual Safety Car was deployed and Norris missed the chance to take advantage, having already passed the pit entry when the alert came through.

McLaren still brought him in on his next tour to remain on the same strategy as Antonelli, both drivers having started on the medium compound, but by that time the VSC had ended and a painfully slow 7s stop dropped him down to P5.

He did manage to recover to the podium, which would normally be a result to celebrate against the likes of Mercedes, but the disappointment was palpable as Norris – and even the triumphant Antonelli – believed that he “deserved” the win.

Hamilton explains brake issues that caused Spanish GP DNF

Ferrari fail to capitalise on strong pace again

The Madring represented an opportunity for Ferrari to capitalise on the circuit's novelty and snatch a good result, especially after a disastrous home event at Monza.

Lewis Hamilton's head-on crash in the final hour of practice gave his mechanics a hefty repair job in order to make Qualifying, but that didn’t seem to dissuade the seven-time World Champion, as he went on to claim provisional pole with the first Q3 flying laps.

Ending up fourth in the final reckoning, directly ahead of team mate Charles Leclerc, there was still a possibility that a podium was on the cards, especially when Hamilton got a superb launch off the line.

Verstappen, who Hamilton had jumped, cut the chicane before eventually allowing the Ferrari driver back ahead, only for Hamilton to suffer a brake problem that sent him through several run-off areas and eventually forced his retirement.

It was a better day for Leclerc, who was likely left questioning what could have been had Ferrari’s hope of a Safety Car or red flag come to fruition. He did not pit under the VSC and thereby inherited the lead, but the lack of any further incidents left him with no choice but to finally pit after 48 laps on the hard tyres.

The gaps that had opened up between the frontrunners and the rest of the top 10 helped the Monegasque to come back out in P4, where he held off Mercedes’ Russell to bring home a respectable haul of points.

Best of the rest for Verstappen after giving positions up

Max Verstappen claimed P2 in Madrid, despite begrudgingly giving back places in the opening laps after tangling with Lewis Hamilton.

The Ferrari driver got ahead after lights out, with Verstappen cutting the first turn by driving off track to keep his P3 starting position.

The Dutchman said on the radio that Hamilton “almost shunted me”, and tried to resist Red Bull's instructions to give the place back to avoid a potential penalty, especially after he had since overtaken Antonelli for P2.

After giving in and allowing both Antonelli and Hamilton through, he quickly returned to the podium places after the Ferrari driver had a problem with his brakes.

Verstappen was also able to make the most of the VSC to limit positions lost during his pit stop, and eventually held off a charging Norris in the closing laps.

Ugochukwu takes F3 title in Madrid

Both F2 and F3 championships were in action at the Madring, with the latter concluding their season in the Spanish city.

Ugo Ugochukwu was up against Freddie Slater for the title, and it was the Campos Racing man who took the crown courtesy of a P2 finish in the final Feature Race.

Slater’s chances were dealt a blow when he was unable to score in the Sprint Race, before failing to finish the first Feature Race, meaning the pair entered the final race tied on points.

Eighth in the second Feature Race was not enough to deny his rival, Ugochukwu taking the title by 14 points in the end, with Tuukka Taponen also left celebrating after taking a maiden F3 victory on Sunday.

Over in F2, Dino Beganovic took a lights-to-flag victory in the Feature Race for DAMS Lucas Oil, as he led home Rodin Motorsport’s Alexander Dunne and Hitech’s Ritomo Miyata.

Championship leader Nikola Tsolov finished down the order, but his rival Rafael Camara could not capitalise, coming home P10 after a penalty to only narrowly reduce his deficit in the standings.

Tsolov leads by seven points, with those two set to resume their rivalry next time out in Baku.

Football stars out in force while Madrid welcomes tennis royalty to the paddock

There were plenty of famous faces from the world of sport on the Madring grid on Sunday, with Real Madrid giving a few players the day off to come and watch F1.

Their manager Jose Mourinho was also on the grid, and having beaten Rayo Vallecano 4-1 in La Liga action the previous evening, he was in an understandably good mood. As was Jude Bellingham, who scored in that match before using his Sunday off to catch up with some of his countrymen.

Vinicius Jnr was seen laughing and joking with Gabriel Bortoleto, while Real Madrid’s goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois towered over some of the drivers – at six foot seven, he is considerably taller than even the likes of Russell and Esteban Ocon.

Footballing legends David Beckham, Zinedine Zidane and Roberto Carlos were also in attendance, as was retired tennis star Rafael Nadal, who was spotted down at Ferrari.

title: What the teams said – Race day in Spain
excerpt:
Mercedes

Kimi Antonelli got a great start from P2, but when challenging for the lead cut the apex of the corner and was forced to cede position. His attempts to do so were messy and he briefly fell behind Verstappen until the Dutchman had to do the same thing. That left Antonelli second, a few seconds behind race leader Norris. But when the Italian got a cheap pit stop under the VSC, he became the de facto leader and from there he kept his race pretty clean to take his eighth win of the year.

As for George Russell, he had contact with Piastri at the start but was lucky to hold on to P6. The team opted to pit him under the VSC too, even though he started on the hards, and then did not think the mediums would last so pitted Russell a second time. That dropped him back again, and he finished fifth.

Kimi Antonelli, 1st

"It was great to get the victory today, but we know we were a little bit fortunate with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car. Lando (Norris) was in control at the front, but we were able to dive into the pits just as the Virtual Safety Car was deployed, make the cheap stop onto the Hard, get the net lead and run to the end. We probably didn’t deserve to win therefore but we will of course take it.

"We can also be happy with our pace today. We know we are still out of step with other teams in terms of upgrades, but we have been able to win the last two races at very different circuits. That is encouraging as we continue the season; we have a good position in the championships but we know there is still a very long way to go."

George Russell, 5th

"No matter what we had done with strategy today we would have finished P5. The Virtual Safety Car came at the worst point for everyone who had started on the Hard tyre like me, and the best point for those who had started on the Medium. Unfortunately, that is how racing goes sometimes but it is a little bit the story of my season so far! It was very difficult to overtake today but I’ve enjoyed driving the Madring overall this weekend.

"It is going to be an intense run to the end of the season. I’m looking forward to getting back to the factory, working with the team, and getting ready for the first of three triple-headers. My pace today, particularly on the Hard tyre, felt good so we can be encouraged by that as we head to Baku."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"We are pleased to have taken the first victory at the Madring; it has been another successful new event for F1 at a great location. Kimi drove well and, whilst the Virtual Safety Car played into his hands, he drove well to bring the car home at what has proved to be a very challenging circuit. To take another win at such a different track to Monza, having not brought a major update package to the car since Canada, is very encouraging.

"On George’s side, he was slightly unfortunate with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car. We started him on the Hard tyre, intending to go long, but we had to take the cheap stop under the Virtual Safety Car and to do something different if we were to try and beat Leclerc. The Ferrari stayed out and we switch George to the Medium but unfortunately it wasn’t the strongest tyre today. George reported early on that he was suffering so we went back to the Hard compound; ultimately whatever we had done we would have come home P5 today.

"We now have one week to get ready for Baku and the beginning of the first of three triple-headers. Extending our lead in the championships is good but we know there is still so much racing to come. It is going to be an intense run to the end of the season but we’re excited for that challenge."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"That was a great result for Kimi and a really strong weekend for the team. We clearly benefited from the timing of the Virtual Safety Car, but credit goes to the drivers and everyone in the garage for being ready to react. The execution of both stops was excellent and that helped us take the win today.

"For Kimi, the decision to pit under the Virtual Safety Car was the one that ultimately put him in the net lead of the race. George's situation was a little more complicated. We had elected to do the opposite of Leclerc strategically because, when you're behind, you often need to try something different to create an opportunity. As the race unfolded, though, it became clear that the Hard tyre was performing better than we had expected and was the compound to be on. That said, if we had mirrored the Ferrari’s strategy, we would have still likely finished P5 with overtaking proving so difficult.

"Ultimately, the Virtual Safety Car arrived at the perfect moment for the cars that could switch onto the Hard tyre, and that's sometimes how racing goes. The important thing is that we've come away with a race win, a strong points haul, and strengthened our position in both championships.

"We'll regroup over the next few days and prepare for the run to the finish of the season. Nine races in 11 weeks is going to be a demanding stretch for everyone, but we've put ourselves in a good position in both title fights and we'll keep pushing right to the final Grand Prix."

title: Wolff explains decision on Russell's tyre strategy in Madrid
excerpt:
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has backed the decision to bring George Russell into the pits twice during the Spanish Grand Prix after the strategy choice was questioned by the driver during the race.

The Briton made two stops during Sunday's event at the Madring on his way to a fifth-placed finish - firstly to change onto a new set of medium tyres during the Virtual Safety Car period and then again onto the hard tyre.

His team mate Kimi Antonelli executed a one-stop strategy, along with the majority of the other teams on the grid, and went on to win the race after Lando Norris lost out due to the timing of the VSC.

Russell was heard on the team radio asking his Race Engineer Marcus Dudley why they had decided to pit twice, saying he could have held off Norris who was behind him at that stage, before going on to finish fifth.

"He [Russell] said the tyres were not in a great shape, the mediums, we didn't think that they would go to the end," he said. "Then the pit opportunity was not to hang out and wait for a red [flag] but to change the tyres and get on with it."

The strategy appeared to have been discussed with Russell following the Grand Prix, who seemed content with the answer after the race whilst speaking to F1 TV.

"In the moment, I was questioning, but, you know, the hard tyre was the superior tyre," he acknowleged. "Maybe I could have stayed out with Leclerc, but I would have still finished behind him.

"Maybe I could have not pitted onto the hard again at the end. But everything I would have done brought us back to the same position, purely because you can’t overtake on this track, so that’s a shame."

In the same interview Russell appeared to rule himself out of winning the Drivers' Championship this season, after Antonelli's win saw him extend his standings lead to 81 points, but Wolff explained they'll work to help him with that mindset.

"You can have good races, bad races, good years and bad years, but we’re talking about a driver who has won everything he could have potentially won before," he said. "Karting championships, Formula 3 in his rookie year, Formula 2 in his rookie year, he went into Williams.

"We need to find out what it is for him to be able to unleash his potential."

title: Stella outlines the logic behind Norris’ ‘unlucky’ stop
excerpt:
McLaren Team Principal Andrea Stella has explained why McLaren opted to pit Lando Norris for fresh tyres just as the Virtual Safety Car period came to an end, admitting that “there was no option to retain the lead” of the Spanish Grand Prix.

With overtaking set to be a challenge at the Madring, Norris had already put himself in a strong position to chase down a potential third victory of the season as he topped Qualifying with a memorable last-gasp effort.

The Briton then succeeded in holding off Kimi Antonelli on the opening lap and gradually eked out a confident advantage over his rivals, managing his tyres until the Virtual Safety Car was deployed to recover Lance Stroll’s stricken Aston Martin.

While Antonelli and Max Verstappen could take advantage and box under the slowed racing conditions, Norris missed out on the opportunity and only headed into the pits as the VSC ended, where he suffered a 7s stop that dropped him to P5.

Despite his driver’s recovery to P3, Stella couldn’t hide the team’s frustration, as he told F1 TV: “Starting from pole position, leading the race and having incredible pace… this would’ve been a race won by many seconds, and we ended up in third position.

“The reality is that in racing, there are elements that you can control and some that you cannot control. The timing of the Virtual Safety Car was a couple of seconds too late – Lando had already passed the pit entry – and then he was a few seconds too early because then it was ending once he came in to pit.”

Asked to elaborate on the reasoning behind the call, Stella said: “The logic is that if you stay out, you stay out with used mediums [that are] already grained, and it means that at some stage you will pit behind the people that have already pitted on the hard tyres, so it’s going to be a similar race to [Charles] Leclerc.

“We would actually have pitted even earlier because the medium would finish earlier, so there was no option really to retain the lead.

“We needed to accept that the timing was incredibly unfortunate and, like I said, it’s a positive race overall.

“The elements that we could not control made a difference but those that we could control make us very optimistic for the future.”

McLaren have made steady gains throughout the season that culminated in Norris’ commanding victories in Hungary and the Netherlands, and this weekend further demonstrated their progress.

Max Verstappen, who only just kept him behind on the closing laps at the Madring, stated that the reigning World Champion was “faster than all of us”, while Antonelli believed that Norris “deserved to win”.

Stella concluded: “Just very unlucky, but I want to think that the positive message of a McLaren [that was] so competitive at a very different circuit layout to Zandvoort and Hungary is very encouraging for the future.

“We take it on the chin. Today we were too fast to win the race because had we been a little slower, we would’ve made it to the pits! We have a smile on our faces, we look forward to the rest of the season.”

title: Leclerc reflects on Ferrari's Spanish GP strategy
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc believes Ferrari "did the right thing" with their strategy decisions during the Spanish Grand Prix, as the Monegasque driver was left out front for much of the race.

Leclerc led 32 of the 57 laps during Formula 1's first visit to the Madring, with Ferrari hopeful that a late-race Safety Car might give their driver a shot at the podium.

But with none forthcoming and George Russell closing to within Leclerc's pit window, Ferrari made the call to pit him on Lap 48 as Leclerc eventually reached the chequered flag in P4.

"I think we did the right thing honestly. If I had to do the race again I would re-do exactly the same thing in terms of strategy," said Leclerc.

"Starting on the soft and doing a soft-hard would have brought me to P4 anyway. Doing a hard-soft, I was just hoping for a Safety Car at the right moment for us at the end, but that never really happened.

"A bit of a shame but at the end we were relying on a bit of the luck and we didn't have it."

Sunday's Grands Prix proved to be a tough outing for Ferrari, as Lewis Hamilton retired as early as Lap 7 with a brake problem.

Hamilton and Leclerc started P4 and P5 respectively after qualifying less than two tenths behind polesitter Lando Norris, but having lacked the outright pace to ultimately start any higher.

Leclerc believes that poor Qualifying performances are putting the Scuderia on the back foot when it comes to Sunday, especially at tracks such as the Hungaroring, Zandvoort and Madring where overtaking is difficult.

"I feel like we are losing the results we want on the Sunday because of a lack of performance on the Saturday. This is where we should focus," he said.

"We need to do a step on the Saturday, especially in Qualifying as we seem to be on the back foot compared to our competitors. Then in the race we are strong but not enough to overtake on track."

title: Verstappen explains Hamilton clash in Spanish GP
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has offered his verdict on the near-miss with Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton on the opening lap of the Spanish Grand Prix, which saw the Dutchman begrudgingly let his rival past after driving off track.

Just as Hamilton got ahead when the lights went out at the Madring, Verstappen cut the first turn and held onto his starting position of P3, provoking calls from the Briton to give the position back.

The Red Bull driver was adamant that Hamilton “almost shunted into me” and tried to resist instructions from the team to avoid a potential penalty, especially as he had also succeeded in passing Kimi Antonelli to take P2.

He soon gave in and allowed both Antonelli and Hamilton through, but quickly returned to the top three as Hamilton began to struggle with his brakes.

“It’s just a bit the nature of the track,” Verstappen said when questioned on the clash. “When you have that track layout with so much tarmac, people of course risk [going] for a move, and I saw what happened – Lewis clipped the kerb so he was going to run wide.

“I think if I would’ve stayed on the track, you touch and there’s a big risk of damage. I decided to drive next to the track, and then of course the team told me to give the position back, which I did. After that, I just tried to do my race.”

He was able to make the most of a Virtual Safety Car and limit the positions lost during his pit stop – something that McLaren’s Lando Norris couldn’t do due to the unfortunate timing, resulting in his eventual result of P3 while Verstappen improved to P2.

Although the four-time World Champion conceded that he didn’t have the performance to match either Norris or race winner Antonelli on his way to claiming his sixth podium of the season, he was satisfied with the weekend as a whole.

“Looking at the race pace, I think it’s a great result,” he said. “Of course, we know that Lando got unlucky with that VSC, so for us I think P2 is an incredible result because you could see how much Lando was catching me.”

He later added: “I think it was quite clear that Lando and Kimi were a lot faster. Once everyone was a little bit clear, it was again the same thing where Kimi was a bit faster than me, Lando was faster than all of us, but I could keep him quite easily behind me.”

title: 'I’m not in the fight for the drivers’ title' – Russell
excerpt:
George Russell appeared to rule himself out of the fight for the Drivers' Championship after Kimi Antonelli claimed his eighth win of the 2026 season in Madrid.

The Briton fell short of his team mate's result again, finishing in P5 in Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix, as the result leaves him 81 points behind in the standings.

After a strong start to the Spanish Grand Prix weekend for the Briton, who topped the first practice session, that was as good as it got as he went on to qualify in P6 and was left questioning his pit stop strategy as Sunday's race unfolded.

After coming home in fifth at the Madring, as his team mate backed up last weekend's heroic home win in Monza with another, Russell appeared to rule himself out of being in contention for this year's title amid Antonelli's form.

"We’re obviously in a great place to win the constructors’," he said. "Realistically, I’m not in the fight for the drivers’, and that just allows me to focus race by race and try to get some good results."

Before the weekend began, the Briton had remarked that Antonelli "had done a better job" but had insinuated he was still in the title fight, though he acknowledged he would need elements of luck to claw back the deficit.

However, that luck didn't materialise during Sunday's Grand Prix as Mercedes opted to pit Russell twice - firstly for a new set of mediums during the Virtual Safety Car and then again onto the hard tyre - when the majority of other teams went for a one-stop strategy.

On the radio Russell asked his Race Engineer Marcus Dudley why they had decided to pit, saying he could have held off Lando Norris behind him. But afterwards, the Briton appeared to have his answers to the strategy call.

"In the moment I was questioning, but the hard tyre was the superior tyre," he acknowledged. "Maybe I could have stayed out with Leclerc, but I would have still finished behind him. Maybe I could have not pitted onto the hard again at the end. But everything I would have done brought us back to the same position, purely because you can’t overtake on this track, so that’s a shame."

Once the favourite to come out on top this season, Russell now heads to Baku with only two Grand Prix wins under his belt in 2026.

He is still in second position in the Drivers' Championship but with seemingly a different mindset that, whilst he is no longer challenging for the individual title, he's keen to make sure the team take home the Constructors' Championship this year.

"It has been a more positive couple of races, even though the result was far from great today," he said. "But it’s kind of the story of the season. I just need to focus on the performance, keep trying to help the team. You know, we’re obviously in a great place to win the Constructors’."

title: Norris 'believes I deserved' Spanish GP victory
excerpt:
Lando Norris believes he "deserved" victory in the Spanish Grand Prix, as an ill-timed Virtual Safety Car contributed to the McLaren driver finishing only third at the chequered flag.

The reigning World Champion started on pole for Formula 1's first race at the Madring and, after rebuffing fellow front-row starter Kimi Antonelli at Turn 1, he built up a comfortable lead in the opening stages.

But Lance Stroll finding the run-off area at Turn 20 prompted a Virtual Safety Car on Lap 15, just as Norris had passed the pit lane entrance, while Antonelli and Max Verstappen pitted behind.

By the time Norris had completed another lap the VSC ended as he headed into the pit lane, where a slow stop meant the Briton lost further time and rejoined down in P5.

It all culminated in Norris challenging Verstappen in the closing laps but falling short of victory to Antonelli by just five seconds.

"The VSC came out after I was already round the last corner," he assessed after the race. "The others were very fortunate today or I was unfortunate, whichever way round you want to look at it.

"Of course, I believe I deserved it today. We did a very good job, I feel like I did everything right this weekend so for it to be lost like today is just pretty crappy.

"It's F1, the race should be won by the best performance and good strategy, maybe going long, things like that.

"Today was just a rule that just benefits some people a lot more than other people. I know that's racing, so I can't be too against it.

"If it was the other way round of course it would suit me, but when I feel like I've driven a perfect weekend and I did such a good job yesterday, and I feel like I did a great job today, it hurts. Nothing I can do."

After a sluggish start under the new-for-2026 regulations, McLaren and Norris have hit their stride this season, with the reigning world champions having taken back-to-back wins in Hungary and Holland, as well as three pole positions from the last four races.

Team Principal Zak Brown had suggested that the title was still possible ahead of the race in Madrid, but the gap now stands at 106 points to Antonelli in the drivers' standings with nine Grands Prix remaining.

"It's only positives this weekend. Apart from I didn't think we were quick enough all weekend until today. I think today we were the best," added Norris.

"As you've seen quite often on Sundays, we take a good step. On Saturdays we're just not where we need to be. We need to understand more what we can do on Saturday.

"I still don't think we have the car that's in a perfect enough condition to fight consistently against the others on Saturday.

"But it seems like on Sunday, the way I drive, the way I can look after the tyres and get lap time out of it, it's giving me a lot of opportunities and I can do a better job than the others.

"That's what's frustrating, there's only positives I can take away from this weekend, there's still things we can work on but we're just very unlucky."

title: Antonelli insists Norris ‘deserved to win’ Spanish GP
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has shared his belief that Lando Norris “deserved to win” the Spanish Grand Prix after the reigning World Champion was forced to settle for third – a poorly-timed Virtual Safety Car impacting his chances of victory.

Norris had taken the challenges of the brand-new Madring in his stride as he executed a superb lap to pip Antonelli to pole position, and despite the Italian’s best efforts, he couldn’t find a way past in the opening stint.

He cut two corners in his attempted overtakes and gradually settled into second place behind Norris, who built a confident advantage at the front of the field before disaster struck for McLaren’s strategy.

A Virtual Safety Car was deployed as Lance Stroll came to a halt with brake issues, handing Mercedes the opportunity to change Antonelli’s tyres without losing as much time as they would in normal conditions.

But Norris had already passed the pit entry when the race was neutralised, and by the time he eventually entered for his stop, the VSC period had ended, dropping him from the lead to P5.

Although the Briton managed to recover back to the podium, Antonelli didn’t feel able to fully celebrate his win due to Norris’ misfortune, as he explained: “It was a very difficult race, not straightforward at all, especially trying to manage tyres.

“It’s good to win, but it doesn’t feel as good because I think Lando today deserved to win. But overall, you know, we’ll take it. Other than that, it was a very strong race. I think especially on the hard [tyres] at the end we had really good pace, and now we’re going to keep pushing.”

The 20-year-old also held off Max Verstappen to secure his eighth Grand Prix triumph of the season, which opened up his lead in the Drivers’ Championship to a commanding 81 points over team mate George Russell.

With nine rounds to go, it’s looking increasingly likely that Antonelli could be crowned the sport's youngest-ever World Champion, but he was adamant that the prospect isn’t on his mind.

Asked if he’s able to start thinking about the title, he replied: “That’s exactly what I don’t want to do. I want to keep pushing race by race, you know, keep delivering and keep enjoying all the way, and then trying to do my best every race, and then we’ll see where we end up at the end of the year.”

title: Oscar Piastri concedes 'going too far' after rare FIA warning
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri has conceded that it was "easy to go too far" after receiving a rare warning from the FIA in the Spanish Grand Prix.

The McLaren driver was handed a black and white flag for exceeding track limits during the race, in which he was carrying damage on the front-wing after first corner contact with George Russell's Mercedes.

As the damage continued to impact the handling and performance of the MCL40, Piastri picked up a rare black and white flag for driving standards as he was deemed to be cutting corners and exceeding track limits.

Reflecting after his eighth-placed finish, his worst since 11th in Canada, Piastri explained how the contact with Russell happened and why he was pushing the boundaries, and picked up the rare flag warning.

"It was just a tough afternoon from literally the start," reflected Piastri to media, including RacingNews365, after his 11th consecutive grand prix without a podium finish.

"From then on, the rest of the race was very compromised, obviously with some of the damage and the track position mainly.

"I was alongside, and he just kept squeezing me to the wall, and then I hit the brakes and kind of avoided him. But amongst all that, he hit the brakes as well. Everyone hit the brakes, and we kind of got stuck together and everything.

"I was just expecting a bit more space, and obviously between a car and a wall, you can't make any more space, so that was tricky.

"On a track like this, you're always searching for a bit of clean air in the high-speed corners, and with no kerb or wall on the inside of some of the corners, it's very easy to just go a little bit too far."

The article continues below.

Piastri's "good race"

Despite finishing eighth, 1m:30s behind team-mate Lando Norris and the last car on the lead lap, Piastri felt he had enjoyed a good race "in clean air" but being stucked in a "train" had cost him after emerging from the pits behind cars, including Franco Colapinto's Alpine, who finished seventh.

"I think the pace and clean air on the hard was pretty good, but we were trying to make up the pit loss of the VSC to the guys who pitted, and once they got the loss back, I was stuck again, so that was painful," said Piastri.

"Then when we pitted onto the medium, we pitted into a four-car train, and that wasn't great, and the medium tyre was just awful.

"It was good for [one lap], and then it was pretty terrible, so a lot of things to try and fix."

title: Liam Lawson reveals 'a lot of risk' behind rare Madring overtake
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has conceded he had to "take a lot of risk" to complete one of the few overtakes of the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring.

The Red Bull driver finished sixth in Madrid, 86.746s behind race winner Andrea Kimi Antonelli, after starting on the hard tyre and running a long first stint.

A virtual safety car worked against him, but Lawson said his weekend had previously been compromised by qualifying. The New Zealander started from eighth on the grid.

Lawson's move on Franco Colapinto, following a change of tyres, was one of the rare passes on a circuit that drew heavy criticism across the weekend from all the drivers.

Organisers have since signalled they are open to layout changes for future editions.

[Article continues below]

'Easy for it to go wrong' - Lawson

Speaking after the race, Lawson confirmed he had also been compromised by a virtual safety car, called on lap 15 after the Aston Martin of Lance Stroll had sustained a brake issue, forcing him to park his car in a run-off area.

"We started on the hard, and that sort of forced us to go a bit longer," said Lawson, speaking to the media, including RacingNews365.

"The VSC wasn't ideal, but considering where we started, I think the damage for us was really done in qualifying, so it's a good result.

"But it's so hard to overtake. I had to take a lot of risk with Franco to make that pass, and I barely, honestly, made the corner without doing track limits. It's just hard with the way this track layout is, but it's fun to qualify on, just difficult to race on.

"Looking at other categories as well, it's obviously quite mental. In F2, F3, there were quite a lot of crashes. It's just easy for it to go wrong."

title: When can Kimi Antonelli win the 2026 F1 drivers' world championship?
excerpt:
When can Kimi Antonelli win the 2026 F1 drivers' championship title?

Following his victory at the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli holds an 81-point lead over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

No other driver is within 100 points of the Italian, who is increasingly set to become the youngest F1 world champion and shatter Sebastian Vettel's record of 23 years, 4 months, 11 days by over three years.

Antonelli, who turned 20 in August 2026, has dominated the season, but when can the Mercedes driver become the first Italian to be crowned world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953?

The article continues below.

THIS ARTICLE WILL BE UPDATED FOLLOWING EVERY GRAND PRIX UNTIL ANTONELLI WINS THE 2026 F1 WORLD DRIVERS' TITLE.

When can Kimi Antonelli win the title?

After the Spanish Grand Prix, there are nine races scheduled to last in the season, each worth 25 points.

This gives a total of 225 points remaining, which climbs to 233 once the eight points on offer in the Singapore Sprint race are added.

When Antonelli's current points lead of 81 is subtracted from this total of 233, it means he needs to score 152 more points to be assured of the title.

As it stands, with an 81 point lead over Russell, Antonelli would win the 2026 F1 drivers' championship title at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with three races scheduled to remain after this, worth 75 points.

However, it is extremely likely that F1 will lose a grand prix from the 2026 schedule, with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix not expected to go ahead owing to the uncertainty in the region due to the Iran War.

Imola is widely expected to fill in as the season finale on December 6th, meaning there are 23 races in the season.

Re-doing the calculations for a 23-race season, after the Spanish Grand Prix, there will be a total of 200 points on offer for race wins, climbing to 208 with the Singapore Sprint.

It means that once Antonelli's lead of 81 points is subtracted from the 208 on offer, he requires only 127 more points to be assured of the title.

With his current points lead of 81 and a 23 race season, Antonelli is on course to win the 2026 F1 world drivers' championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix on November 1st.

He would be 20 years, 2 months, 8 days on this date.

title: McLaren boss bemoans 'cruelty' that struck Lando Norris
excerpt:
McLaren chief executive Zak Brown believed Lando Norris was hit by "cruel" luck after being denied a Spanish Grand Prix victory by an ill-timed safety car.

From a "masterpiece" of a pole position at the Madring, a word used by McLaren team principal Andrea Stella to describe his driver's out-of-nowhere lap, Norris comfortably led the opening 14 laps.

However, an incident involving Aston Martin's Lance Stroll sparked a virtual safety car. Unfortunately for Norris, he missed the window by five seconds, whilst behind him, Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen both pitted.

Norris then pitted just as the VSC ended, coming out fifth behind leader Charles Leclerc in his Ferrari, Antonelli, Verstappen and the second Mercedes of George Russell.

After Mercedes opted to pit Russell for a second time, and Leclerc pitted late on, Norris moved up to third, and despite hounding Verstappen over the closing laps, around a track where it proved almost impossible to pass, the Briton had to settle for that place as Antonelli took the chequered flag.

Asked about the racing gods not smiling on Norris, speaking on Sky Sports F1, Brown said: "They were cruel today - twice!

"I mean, Lando was gone; the team did a great job. The VSC came out a couple of seconds after Lando had gone by, and then went away a couple of seconds before we pit. There's nothing we could have done.

"[But] Great to hear Lando's radio message, we just shrug it off. I think that was our race by 20-25 seconds."

[Article continues below]

'We were too quick' - Norris

On the cool-down lap after the race, Norris was quickly on the radio to his team, recognising the cruelty of his situation.

"We take it on the chin," remarked Norris. "We were too quick. That's all it was. Very unlucky today, guys. We deserved the win quite easily, so a big thank you.

"I didn't think we were going to have a chance here. We should have won. All right, guys, keep it going. I'll keep delivering. Keep working hard. We can still win plenty more races this year."

Brown stated that Norris "was dominant" around the Madring. He added: "He was gone. Managing it, great; tyre wear was great. Yeah, he was in a league of his own. It's just unfortunate.

"He's got a trophy, but it's a P3, not a P1."

title: Toto Wolff thankful to 'racing gods' as Kimi Antonelli steals Spanish GP win
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has explained how the "racing gods" were on the side of Kimi Antonelli during his fortunate Spanish Grand Prix victory.

Antonelli inherited the lead at the Madring after a fortunately timed pit-stop under the virtual safety car for Lance Stroll's stopped Aston Martin.

Race leader Norris just missed the pit entry under VSC conditions, with Antonelli pitting under the caution, with Norris doing so once the race had gone green next time around, but the world champion lost 20 seconds of race time in pitting under green conditions.

This meant both Antonelli and Max Verstappen undercut Norris, with the Italian cycling to the lead once Charles Leclerc pitted, having run long for the Ferrari.

The victory, the eighth of the season for the 20-year-old, means he has now opened up a 81-point lead over team-mate Geroge Russell, who finished fifth.

Antonelli has now won more grands prix - eight - in 2026 than Russell has in his career, seven.

Reflecting on the race, Wolff broke down the sequence of events.

Toto Wolff thankful to 'racing gods' as Kimi Antonelli steals Spanish GP win

"I think we've been mostly unlucky with virtual safety cars, and safety cars this year," Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

"Today the race gods were with us. We literally pulled Kimi in when the VSC came out, and it is unfortunate for McLaren because they were fast. But Kimi drove very, very well."

The article continues below.

Wolff on Mercedes' decision to pit

With just a few seconds to decide to pit Antonelli under the VSC, Wolff spoke of the "three seconds" the team had to make its decision.

"The process was great today. The strategy group had the VSC on their mind.

"Someone said: 'the Aston Martin won’t clear quickly’ and it was strategy to Peter Bonnington, Bono double-checked, and Bono to Kimi.

"All of that talking within three seconds."

title: Lando Norris fires back after bizarre Spanish GP 'cola' incident
excerpt:
Lando Norris fired back after being told not to drink a can of Coca-Cola in Formula 1's cooldown room following the Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring.

The reigning world champion started on pole and was looking set to claim a comfortable victory before becoming the latest victim of virtual safety car timing.

Lance Stroll pulled off the circuit with brake issues in the final sector, resulting in a virtual safety car – the race's only interruption in the Spanish capital.

Unfortunately for Norris, he had just passed the pit entry as the VSC was confirmed, while it ended before the conclusion of the following lap.

It cost the McLaren driver significantly, as Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen behind both benefitted from pitting during the VSC, losing less time than they would have during a normal stop.

Due to having to take a normal pit stop later in the race, Norris fell from first to third, where he went on to finish.

Norris was frustrated after the race having lost a likely win, and was seen on the broadcast drinking a can of Coca-Cola in the cooldown room.

The soft drink brand is not a sponsor of F1, which holds a deal with its biggest rival, PepsiCo. It is, however, a sponsor of McLaren.

While drinking the beverage in the cooldown room, Norris appeared to be told to put the Coca-Cola away, with Antonelli also indicating that he should hide the label.

Norris was having none of it and responded to the individual querying the Coca-Cola: "I just did a race, so I'm allowed to drink what I would like. Thank you so much."

Fans have quickly taken to social media to praise the Briton's response, defending his right to drink whatever he chooses after a gruelling race.

title: Lewis Hamilton explains cause of first Ferrari retirement in 10 months
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has explained the sequence of events behind his brake failure that led to his retirement from the Spanish Grand Prix.

Hamilton retired on Lap 7 of 57 in Madrid after the SF-26 machine suffered a brake failure, with Hamilton going off at Turn 20 as he struggled to slow the Ferrari down after early battles with Max Verstappen.

Hamilton had been the only driver to complete every grand prix and Sprint race lap in 2026 prior to the retirement, which is his first since the 2025 Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

It is the first time since the 2014 Canadian Grand Prix that Hamilton has suffered a brakes-related retirement, and is the 35th retirement of his career in his 394th start.

"I had a good start, I didn't see Max, and I wasn't in the battle going down to Turn 5," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365.

"But then I went into Turn 5, I hit the brake, and it started stopping okay, and then the pedal took a step, and it wouldn't stop all of a sudden.

"I ended up going wide, and that's when I tapped the barrier, but it didn't really feel bad, like a bad touch.

"Then the pedal came back, and it was fine for the next corners, and things were looking okay, and then the pedal went long."

The article continues below.

Hamilton addresses Verstappen battle

As for Verstappen's complaints about the move at Turn 1, when presented with what the Red Bull driver had said, Hamilton offered a short reply.

"Well, I thought it was pretty good racing, to be honest," the Ferrari driver replied.

title: Max Verstappen issues comical response to successful Lando Norris defence
excerpt:
Max Verstappen issued a comical response when asked how he successfully kept Lando Norris behind him in the closing laps of the Spanish Grand Prix, held at the Madring.

The Dutchman started from third but gained a position to secure an impressive second-place finish, more than was expected of Red Bull heading into the event.

It was an eventful start for Verstappen, who cut the opening corner, passing Lewis Hamilton and race winner Kimi Antonelli in the process.

Red Bull instructed Verstappen to return both positions, something the four-time world champion did after initially complaining.

Hamilton's retirement promoted the 28-year-old back into third, before he rose to second after Norris was unable to pit during a virtual safety car period while leading the race. Verstappen did pit.

Fresher tyres allowed Norris to catch Verstappen in the closing laps, yet the reigning world champion was unable to find a way past.

"Looking at the race pace, for us, a great result," said Verstappen.

"Lando got unlucky with the VSC, so for us P2 is an incredible result because you could see how much he was catching me but around here you can't pass, so I could keep him behind."

Verstappen Madring criticism continues after strong podium

Verstappen has been critical of the Madring's layout throughout the weekend, mostly because it does not feature an overtaking opportunity.

That, in itself, made defending simple for Red Bull's star driver.

Asked how he kept Norris behind, Verstappen explained: "Just keep the car in the middle.

"That works quite well around here and just trying to keep the grip in the tyres, which was the hardest part of that stint."

title: Kimi Antonelli makes Lando Norris concession after fortunate Spanish victory
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has conceded that Lando Norris deserved to win the Spanish Grand Prix, but declared "we'll take it" after a fortunate virtual safety car.

Antonelli now holds an 81-point advantage over George Russell, who finished in fifth place following his eighth win of the season.

It means Antonelli is likely to be leading the championship by the time F1 arrives in Austin for the United States Grand Prix, with 83 points on offer across the Azerbaijan-Bahrain-Singapore races, with Singapore being a Sprint.

Antonelli's win came after he was able to pit behind a virtual safety car for Lance Stroll's stopped Aston Martin, with leader Norris having just missed the pit entry under the VSC conditions.

By the time Norris pitted, the race had resumed under green flag conditions, meaning Antonelli and Max Verstappen were able to get ahead.

In the end, Antonelli won by 4.3s from Verstappen with Norris in third, and beat Russell by 29.8s as he took a giant leap towards becoming the youngest world champion in F1 history.

Reflecting after the record-equalling 251st win for a Mercedes engine, Antonelli made clear that he felt Norris was the best driver on the day.

"It was a very difficult race, not straightforward at all, especially trying to manage tyres, but I think today it is good to win, but it doesn't feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win," Antonelli said.

"But overall we'll take it. And other than that, it was a very strong race. I think, especially on the hard at the end, we had really good pace.

"Now we're going to keep pushing. I want to keep pushing race by race, keep delivering and keep enjoying it all the way, and I'm trying to do my best every race, and then we'll see where we end up at the end of the year."

title: Kimi Antonelli delivers latest F1 title blow as Lewis Hamilton suffers brake failure at Spanish GP
excerpt:
Victory number eight of the season for Kimi Antonelli, who has further extended his championship lead!

Kimi Antonelli has won the Spanish Grand Prix, taking his eighth victory of the 2026 F1 campaign.

The Mercedes driver has further extended his championship advantage, crossing the line ahead of Max Verstappen and Lando Norris.

It was a disastrous race for seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, who was forced to retire his car early on after suffering a brake failure.

His team-mate Charles Leclerc led for much of the race after staying out under a virtual safety car, but was forced to concede the lead to Antonelli late on.

Kimi Antonelli delivers latest F1 title blow as Lewis Hamilton suffers brake failure at Spanish GP

# Driver Team Time Tyre

Results are being loaded...

Norris maintains early control

On the opening lap, Norris held onto the lead while Antonelli attacked, running off the track on two occasions while doing so.

As a result, he was forced to give up his position to Norris, having moved ahead off the circuit - but as he did so, Verstappen managed to slip through.

But Verstappen himself was asked to give his place back to Hamilton, forcing the Dutchman to lose two positions as he also had to allow Antonelli through in the process.

Soon after, though, Hamilton’s race would come completely undone, as a brake issue forced him to retire from the grand prix.

Up front, Norris stretched out his lead across the opening 10 laps, pulling himself well clear of Antonelli.

However, the race would soon be turned on its head, as Lance Stroll also noted brake issues of his own, which saw him end the race in the wall.

Virtual safety car results in McLaren pain

A virtual safety car was then called, which saw much of the field come in for a pit stop.

Unfortunately for Norris, it was called right after he passed the pit lane entry, allowing Antonelli and the rest to get a cheap pit stop.

Norris pitted the next time around, but at that stage the virtual safety car had ended, which dropped Norris to fifth place after his stop.

To add insult to injury, he suffered a slow stop - ensuring he rejoined behind Leclerc, Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell.

Leclerc was the only driver in the front-running pack who did not elect to take a pit stop under the virtual safety car as Ferrari targeted a one-stop strategy.

Norris was able to gain a position when Russell pitted on lap 29 and spent the next handul of laps closing in on Verstappen for third.

Verstappen came under significant pressure from Norris in the final laps, however, the Dutchman held on to take the runner-up spot.

Leclerc had to settle for fourth place, while Russell took sixth on the road in the second Mercedes.

After a disappointing outing last time out in Italy, Liam Lawson returned to the points - albeit in a rather lonely sixth place.

Franco Colapinto consolidated another strong result with a run to seventh place, leading Oscar Piastri across the line, who suffered another turbulent race for McLaren.
